questions.q: What is the essay's central argument?
options: Organizations are the surest path to success for ambitious people
Capitalism's rules are what make outcomes so unequal, and should change
Returns for performance are superlinear, which ambitious people should understand
Effort is always rewarded in direct proportion to what you put in
questions.explain: The author says returns for performance are superlinear, stemming from exponential growth and thresholds.

questions.q: What are the two fundamental causes of superlinear returns?
options: Capital accumulation and cheap labor
Competition and sheer luck in markets
Exponential growth and thresholds
Network effects and social prestige
questions.explain: The author says they reduce to exponential growth and thresholds.

questions.q: What does Y Combinator encourage founders to focus on?
options: Growth rate
Number of employees
Absolute revenue numbers
Fundraising amounts
questions.explain: YC encourages focusing on growth rate rather than absolute numbers.

questions.q: Why did prestige used to track organizations, according to the author?
options: Organizations paid their members far more than independents
Individuals were legally forbidden from working on their own
Governments licensed ambitious work only through large institutions
Without an organization you were unlikely to achieve much
questions.explain: In 1970 organizations were the only source of resources, colleagues and distribution.

questions.q: Why is Silicon Valley tolerant of failure, per the author?
options: Failure thresholds there are easy for anyone to cross
Investors there are insured against losing their money
It treats failure itself as an achievement worth celebrating
Failures that involve learning are still compounding
questions.explain: It will keep betting on you only if you're learning from failures, since learning compounds.
